entries.name: Implant Dragon-like Heart
entries: The heart must be implanted through a surgical procedure performed by a skilled medical practitioner. No magical ritual is required.

At the conclusion of the procedure, you must make a DC 12 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the implantation fails and the heart is destroyed. On a successful save, the heart is permanently implanted within your body, granting you attunement to it.

A creature can have only one dragon heart implanted within its body at a time. A new dragon heart can be implanted to replace an existing one, but the previously implanted heart is destroyed in the process. Once implanted, a dragon heart cannot be removed by any means short of a {@spell wish} spell.

entries.name: Damage Absorption
entries: Whenever you take damage of the damage type associated with your dragon-like heart, reduce that damage by an amount equal to your proficiency bonus.

entries.name: Dragon Breath (Recharge 5-6)
entries: As an action, you exhale elemental energy in either a 15-foot cone or a 30-foot line that is 5 feet wide (your choice). Each creature in that cone or line must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking a number of d4s equal to your primary ability modifier in elemental damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The element of the dragon's heart determines the damage type of the exhalation.

entries.name: Elemental of the Dragon
entries: Once per round, when you cast a spell or use an ability that deals damage of your attuned damage type, you deal extra damage equal to a number of d4s equal to your primary ability modifier.

entries.name: Dragon Scale
entries: Your scales harden, granting you a natural armor class of 14. In addition, your unarmed strikes deal 1d4 slashing damage.

entries.name: Implant Wyrmling Heart Ritual
entries: To obtain a wyrmling heart capable of undergoing this ritual, the heart must first be carefully extracted intact from the body of a wyrmling dragon. The extraction must be performed without damaging the heart in any way.

Once obtained, the wyrmling heart must be enchanted through a ritual performed by a willing spellcaster who possesses knowledge of the ritual. The ritual takes 4 hours to perform and must be completed in its entirety.

At the conclusion of the ritual, you must make a DC 16 Wisdom or Charisma saving throw (your choice). On a failed save, the ritual fails and the wyrmling heart is destroyed. On a successful save, the wyrmling heart becomes enchanted and is permanently implanted within your body, granting you attunement to the heart.

A creature can have only one dragon heart implanted within its body at a time. A new dragon heart can be implanted to replace an existing one, but the previously implanted heart is destroyed in the process. Once implanted, a dragon heart cannot be removed by any means short of a {@spell wish} spell.

entries.name: Damage Absorption
entries: You have resistance against the heart's damage type.

entries.name: Dragon Breath (Recharge 5-6)
entries: As an action, you exhale elemental energy in either a 30-foot cone or a 60-foot line that is 5 feet wide (your choice). Each creature in that cone or line must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking a number of d6s equal to your primary ability modifier in elemental damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The element of the dragon's heart determines the damage type of the exhalation.

entries.name: Elemental of the Dragon
entries: Twice per round, when you cast a spell or use an ability that deals damage of your attuned damage type, you deal extra damage equal to a number of d6s equal to your primary ability modifier.

entries.name: Dragon Scale
entries: Your scales harden, granting you a natural armor class of 16. In addition, your unarmed strikes deal 1d6 slashing damage.

entries.name: Dragon Sense
entries: You have blindsight out to a range of 10 feet.

entries.name: Dragon Wings
entries: You can fly at half your walking speed.

entries.name: Implant Dragon Heart Ritual
entries: To obtain a dragon heart capable of undergoing this ritual, the heart must first be carefully extracted intact from the body of a dragon. The extraction must be performed without damaging the heart in any way.

Once obtained, the ancient dragon heart must be enchanted through a ritual performed by a willing dragon or another creature with equivalent knowledge and expertise in the ritual. The ritual takes 1 day to perform and must be completed in its entirety.

A creature can have only one dragon heart implanted within its body at a time. A new dragon heart can be implanted to replace an existing one, but the previously implanted heart is destroyed in the process. Once implanted, a dragon heart cannot be removed by any means short of a {@spell wish} spell.

entries.name: Damage Absorption
entries: You have immunity to the damage type associated with your dragon heart.

entries.name: Dragon Breath (Recharge 5-6)
entries: As an action, you exhale elemental energy in either a 60-foot cone or a 120-foot line that is 10 feet wide (your choice). Each creature in that cone or line must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking a number of d8s equal to your primary ability modifier in elemental damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The element of the dragon's heart determines the damage type of the exhalation.

entries.name: Elemental of the Dragon
entries: A number of times per round equal to your proficiency bonus, when you cast a spell or use an ability that deals damage of your attuned damage type, you deal extra damage equal to a number of d8s equal to your primary ability modifier.

entries.name: Dragon Scale
entries: Your scales harden, granting you a base AC of 18. In addition, your unarmed strikes deal 1d8 slashing damage.

entries.name: Dragon Sense
entries: You have blindsight out to a range of 30 feet and truesight out to a range of 10 feet.

entries.name: Dragon Wings
entries: You can fly at a speed equal to your walking speed.

entries.name: Draconic Lifeforce
entries: You age at a slower rate. For every 10 years that pass, your body ages only 1 year, and you are immune to being magically aged.

entries.name: Dragon Heart Ritual
entries: To obtain a dragon heart capable of undergoing this ritual, the heart must first be carefully extracted intact from the body of an ancient dragon. The extraction must be performed without damaging the heart in any way.

Once obtained, the ancient dragon heart must be enchanted through a ritual performed by a willing ancient dragon who possesses knowledge of the ritual. The ritual takes 1 day to perform and must be completed in its entirety.

At the conclusion of the ritual, you must make a DC 20 Wisdom or Charisma saving throw (your choice). On a failed save, the ritual fails and the dragon heart is destroyed. On a successful save, the dragon heart becomes enchanted and is permanently implanted within your body, granting you attunement to the heart.

A creature can have only one dragon heart implanted within its body at a time. A new dragon heart can be implanted to replace an existing one, but the previously implanted heart is destroyed in the process. Once implanted, a dragon heart cannot be removed by any means short of a {@spell wish} spell.

entries.name: Damage Absorption
entries: You have immunity to the damage type associated with your dragon heart. Whenever you are subjected to damage of that type, you take none of that damage and regain a number of hit points equal to half the damage dealt.

entries.name: Dragon Breath (Recharge 5-6)
entries: As an action, you exhale elemental energy in either a 90-foot cone or a 180-foot line that is 10 feet wide (your choice). Each creature in that cone or line must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking a number of d10s equal to your primary ability modifier in elemental damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The element of the dragon's heart determines the damage type of the exhalation.

entries.name: Elemental of the Dragon
entries: When you cast a spell or use an ability that deals damage of your attuned damage type, you deal an extra d10s damage equal to your primary ability modifier.

entries.name: Dragon Scale
entries: Your scales harden, granting you a natural armor class of 20. In addition, your unarmed strikes deal 1d10 slashing damage.

entries.name: Draconic Lifeforce
entries: You age at a slower rate. For every 10 years that pass, your body ages only 1 year, and you are immune to being magically aged.

entries.name: Dragon Sense
entries: You have blindsight out to a range of 120 feet and truesight out to a range of 30 feet.

entries.name: Dragon Wings
entries: You can fly at a speed equal to twice your walking speed.

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (1/Day)
entries: If you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Great Wyrm Heart Ritual
entries: To obtain a Great Wyrm heart capable of undergoing this ritual, the heart must first be carefully extracted intact from the body of a Great Wyrm. The extraction must be performed without damaging the heart in any way.

Once obtained, the Great Wyrm heart must be enchanted through a ritual performed by a willing Great Wyrm or another creature with equivalent knowledge and expertise in the ritual. The ritual takes 7 days to perform and must be completed in its entirety.

At the conclusion of the ritual, you must make a DC 24 Wisdom or Charisma saving throw (your choice). On a failed save, the ritual fails and the Great Wyrm heart is destroyed. On a successful save, the Great Wyrm heart becomes enchanted and is permanently implanted within your body, granting you attunement to the heart.

A creature can have only one dragon heart implanted within its body at a time. A new dragon heart can be implanted to replace an existing one, but the previously implanted heart is destroyed in the process. Once implanted, a dragon heart cannot be removed by any means short of a {@spell wish} spell.

entries.name: Damage Absorption
entries: You have immunity to the damage type associated with your Great Wyrm heart. Whenever you are subjected to damage of that type, you take none of that damage and regain hit points equal to the amount of damage prevented.

entries.name: Dragon Breath (Recharge 5-6)
entries: As an action, you exhale elemental energy in either a 120-foot cone or a 240-foot line that is 15 feet wide (your choice). Each creature in that cone or line must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking a number of d12s equal to your primary ability modifier in elemental damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The element of the Great Wyrm heart determines the damage type of the exhalation.

entries.name: Elemental of the Dragon
entries: When you cast a spell or use an ability that deals damage of your attuned damage type, you deal extra damage equal to a number of d12s equal to your primary ability modifier.

entries.name: Dragon Scale
entries: Your scales harden, granting you a base AC of 24. In addition, your unarmed strikes deal 1d12 slashing damage.

entries.name: Draconic Lifeforce
entries: You age at a slower rate. For every 10 years that pass, your body ages only 1 year, and you are immune to being magically aged.

entries.name: Dragon Sense
entries: You have blindsight out to a range of 240 feet and truesight out to a range of 120 feet.

entries.name: Dragon Wings
entries: You can fly at a speed equal to three times your walking speed.

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: If you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead. You can use this property three times per day.

entries.name: Great Wyrm's Arcane Legacy
entries: When you finish a long rest, choose one spell from the Sorcerer spell list of any level. The chosen spell is stored within your Great Wyrm heart and does not count against your number of spells known.
You can cast the stored spell once without expending a spell slot. Once you cast the spell in this way, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.
Whenever you finish a long rest, you can choose a different spell from the Sorcerer spell list to replace the stored spell.
If the stored spell can be cast at a higher level, it is always cast as a 9th-level spell when cast using this feature, regardless of its normal level.

Your primary ability modifier is used for the spellcasting ability of spells cast through this feature. Your spell save DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your primary ability modifier, and your spell attack bonus equals your proficiency bonus + your primary ability modifier.

entries.name: Doorway to Anywhere
entries: As an action, you place the door against a solid surface and speak the name or clearly describe a destination on the same plane of existence. The door opens onto an unoccupied space at that destination, provided you have been there before or can describe it well enough for the DM to identify it. The opening is 5 feet wide and 8 feet tall.

The door remains open for up to 1 minute, or until you close it as a bonus action. Creatures can move through it in either direction. The door cannot open into a space occupied by a creature or solid object.
Once you use this property, it cannot be used again until the next dawn. The door does not bypass magical effects that specifically prevent teleportation or planar travel, at the DM's discretion.

entries.name: Uncertain Destinations
entries: If the destination is on another plane, the door does not open and the use is wasted. The door cannot open to a location you cannot physically fit through, such as a sealed space with no available volume.

entries.name: Rotor Flight
entries: As a bonus action, you attach the Take-copter to your head. While wearing it, you gain a flying speed of 30 feet and can hover. The Take-copter carries you and your worn or carried equipment, but it cannot lift another creature.

The Take-copter functions for up to 1 hour, divided as you choose into increments of at least 1 minute. It regains all expended flight time daily at dawn. If its flight time expires while you are airborne, it lowers you safely at a rate of 60 feet per round until you reach the ground.

entries.name: Temporal Travel
entries: The Time Machine can travel through time along the timeline of its current plane. It can carry up to eight willing creatures, including the pilot, plus their carried equipment. Operating it requires 10 minutes of uninterrupted control and a clear intended date or historical event.

The DM determines whether the chosen destination is reachable and what consequences temporal travel creates. The machine cannot guarantee that history can be changed, and major changes may create paradoxes, alternate timelines, or other campaign-level consequences determined by the DM.
Travel to a different plane is not possible unless the DM establishes that the machine has been modified to do so.

entries.name: Temporal Coordinates
entries: The machine can return to a temporal destination it has previously visited. It records up to ten such destinations. Recording or replacing a destination requires 1 minute while the machine is present at that point in time.

entries.name: Artifact Nature
entries: The Time Machine cannot be permanently destroyed by ordinary damage. If reduced to 0 hit points, it becomes inoperable and repairs itself after 7 days, reappearing at the last safe temporal destination it recorded.

entries.name: Imprinted Knowledge
entries: As an action, press a slice of Memory Bread against a page or other flat surface bearing visible writing, symbols, or a diagram. The bread copies the visible information. A creature that eats the slice within 1 hour perfectly recalls the copied information for the next 24 hours.

The bread can copy up to one page of ordinary writing or one diagram that fits within a 1-foot square. It cannot copy magical secrets, encode meaning the eater cannot understand, or grant proficiency in a skill or tool. After 24 hours, the supernatural recall fades, though the creature may retain ordinary memories of what it learned.

entries.name: Limited Supply
entries: A package contains 10 slices. Each slice loses its magic once used or after 24 hours outside its sealed package.

entries.name: Enlarge
entries: As an action, target one Small or larger creature or one nonmagical object you can see within 30 feet. An unwilling creature can make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, avoiding the effect on a success. On a failure, or if the target is willing, the target's size increases by one category for 10 minutes, to a maximum of Huge.

A creature enlarged this way has advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws, and its equipment grows with it. Its weapons deal an extra 1d4 damage. The target's space and reach change as appropriate for its new size. This effect does not stack with itself.
The light has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. Each use expends 1 charge.

entries.name: Reduce
entries: As an action, target one Small or larger creature or one nonmagical object you can see within 30 feet. An unwilling creature can make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, avoiding the effect on a success. On a failure, or if the target is willing, the target's size decreases by one category for 10 minutes, to a minimum of Tiny.

A creature reduced this way has disadvantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws, and its equipment shrinks with it. Its weapon attacks deal 1d4 less damage (minimum 1 damage). The target's space and reach change as appropriate for its new size. This effect does not stack with itself.
The light has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. Each use expends 1 charge.

entries.name: Universal Translation
entries: As a bonus action, eat a piece of Translation Jelly. For 8 hours, you can understand the literal meaning of any spoken language you hear and any written language you touch, and creatures that understand at least one language can understand your speech.

This property does not decode secret messages, ciphers, or deliberately concealed meanings, and it does not allow you to speak with creatures that have no language. A creature must consume its own piece to gain the effect.

entries.name: Supply
entries: A jar contains 6 pieces. Each piece loses its magic once eaten.

entries.name: Phase Opening
entries: As an action, place the hoop against a nonmagical solid surface no thicker than 10 feet. The hoop creates a circular opening 5 feet in diameter through that surface, connecting the two sides. The opening lasts for 10 minutes or until you remove the hoop as a bonus action.

The opening does not damage the surface and cannot pass through a creature or an artifact. If the surface is thicker than 10 feet, the property fails without expending a use. Once used, the hoop cannot be used again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Safe Passage
entries: The opening is a physical passage, not teleportation. Creatures and objects can pass through it normally, and effects that block teleportation do not prevent passage.

entries.name: Friendship Dumplings
entries: As an action, offer a creature a piece of Momotaro Dango. A beast that eats it becomes friendly toward you and your companions for 8 hours, provided you or your companions have not harmed it in the previous 24 hours. The effect ends early if you or your companions attack it.

The dumpling does not charm a creature, control its actions, or force it to obey commands. A creature that refuses to eat the dumpling is unaffected. The DM decides whether a creature is physically capable of eating it.

entries.name: Supply
entries: A pouch contains 4 dumplings. Each dumpling loses its magic once eaten.

entries.name: Extradimensional Storage
entries: The pocket opens into an extradimensional space that can hold up to 10,000 pounds of objects, not exceeding 1,000 cubic feet. The pocket always weighs 1 pound regardless of its contents. Placing an object inside or retrieving it requires an action.

Living creatures can enter the pocket only if they can fit through its opening. The pocket contains breathable air for up to 10 minutes total, divided among creatures inside. After that time, creatures inside begin suffocating. The pocket is not a safe shelter from spells or effects that target extradimensional spaces.

entries.name: Instant Retrieval
entries: As a bonus action, you can retrieve one object from the pocket if you know that it is inside and can describe it. If several objects match the description, the DM determines which one you retrieve.

While attuned to the pocket, you can place or retrieve objects even when the pocket is full, provided the object you are retrieving is already inside. The pocket cannot contain another extradimensional storage item; placing one inside causes both items and their contents to spill harmlessly into the nearest unoccupied spaces.

entries.name: Artifact Nature
entries: The pocket cannot be permanently destroyed by ordinary damage. If it is torn or otherwise disabled, its contents remain in stasis in the extradimensional space and the pocket repairs itself after 7 days.

entries.name: Compressed-Air Blast
entries: As an action, make a ranged weapon attack with the cannon against one creature or object within 60 feet. You are proficient with this attack. On a hit, the target takes 2d8 force damage and, if it is Large or smaller, must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or be pushed 10 feet away from you.
The cannon has 6 charges and regains 1d6 expended charges daily at dawn. Each shot expends 1 charge. The cannon makes no sound louder than a sharp pop.

entries.name: Invisible Wearer
entries: As an action, pull the cloak over yourself. You become invisible until you remove the cloak, attack, or cast a spell. The cloak cannot make objects you carry invisible unless they are fully concealed beneath it.
Once this property ends, it cannot be used again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Temporal Transformation
entries: As an action, you can wrap the Time Cloth around a creature or object that fits within a 10-foot cube. The cloth can affect a creature, an egg, a seed, a damaged object, or another suitable target.
When you wrap a target, choose one of the following effects: Reverse Time, Advance Time, or Restore Condition.

entries.name: Reverse Time
entries: The target returns to an earlier stage of its existence. You choose how far back in time the target reverts, up to 100 years. A creature can return to an earlier age or developmental stage, such as an adult becoming a child or a hatched creature returning to its unhatched state if its body can undergo that transformation. The target retains its memories, personality, class features, and other abilities unless the DM determines that a particular change makes this impossible.

An object returns to an earlier physical state, repairing ordinary damage or restoring missing pieces that existed at the chosen point in time. This property cannot restore a destroyed artifact or recreate a consumed magic item.

entries.name: Advance Time
entries: The target advances through time by up to 100 years. A living creature ages and develops naturally for the chosen period, while an egg or seed can progress through its natural stages of development. An object undergoes the natural passage of time, such as a seed growing into a plant or fresh food spoiling.

This effect does not grant a creature additional class levels, experience, knowledge, or magical power merely because time has passed. The DM determines the result when accelerated development depends on nutrition, environmental conditions, or other requirements.

entries.name: Restore Condition
entries: The target returns to a previous physical condition from any point within the last 100 years. The cloth can repair ordinary damage, restore broken pieces, or return a living creature to a previous stage of physical development. It cannot restore a creature to life if the creature is dead, and it cannot restore expended spell slots or other magical resources.

entries.name: Limitations
entries: The Time Cloth cannot affect a target larger than a 10-foot cube. A creature can resist being affected by succeeding on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw. An unconscious or willing creature can choose to fail this saving throw.

Once the Time Cloth has been used, it cannot be used again until the next dawn. The DM determines the precise outcome of transformations that would fundamentally alter a creature's life cycle or the history of an object.

entries.name: Perfect Duplication
entries: As an action, hold a nonliving object in front of the mirror. The mirror creates an exact duplicate of that object in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. The duplicate reproduces the original object's physical properties, materials, magical properties, charges, and remaining duration, if any.

The mirror can duplicate any nonliving object, including magic items, provided the original object is of Legendary rarity or lower. The mirror cannot duplicate artifacts, creatures, or objects that are part of a creature's body.

The duplicate is a separate object and functions normally, except that its left and right sides are reversed. Text, symbols, designs, and other directional features are mirrored. This reversal does not alter the object's magical properties unless those properties specifically depend on its orientation.

A duplicated magic item retains its normal properties and does not require additional attunement beyond the requirements that would normally apply to that item. If the item requires attunement, the duplicate must be attuned to separately.

entries.name: Limitations
entries: The mirror cannot duplicate artifacts, living creatures, souls, or magical effects that have no physical object as their source. It cannot duplicate a unique entity merely by reflecting its appearance.
The duplicate persists normally and does not disappear after a time limit. Once the mirror creates a duplicate, it cannot be used again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Exile from the World
entries: As an action, press the switch while pointing at one creature or object you can see within 60 feet. The target must make a DC 19 Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the target vanishes from its current plane of existence and is transported to a random location on a random plane of existence. On a success, the target is unaffected.

The destination is determined by the DM, who chooses a random plane and a random location within that plane. The destination can be anywhere, including a hostile environment, an uninhabited world, or a location from which returning may be extremely difficult. The switch does not guarantee the target's survival at the destination.

An affected creature takes everything it is wearing and carrying with it. The target is not killed or incapacitated by the switch itself, and time continues to pass normally for it in the destination plane.

A creature transported by this property can return by any means capable of planar travel, such as plane shift or a similar effect, if it can determine its destination and satisfy the requirements of that effect. The switch does not provide a way to return.

entries.name: Limitations
entries: The switch cannot transport an artifact or a deity. An object that is not being worn or carried by a creature is transported along with any objects contained within it, provided the DM considers them part of the target.
A creature that succeeds on its saving throw is immune to the Dictator Switch for 24 hours.
Once this property has been used, it cannot be used again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Stop Time
entries: As an action, you stop time for everyone except yourself for up to 1 minute. During this interval, you can move and take actions normally, but you cannot affect or move an object worn or carried by another creature, and your actions have no effect on them until time resumes. You cannot use this property to damage a creature while time is stopped.
When the duration ends, time resumes and any effects you created that can persist normally take effect. The watch cannot be activated while time is already stopped by this property.
Once you use this property, roll a d6 at the end of each long rest. The watch regains its use on a roll of 5 or 6.

entries.name: Artifact Nature
entries: The watch cannot be permanently destroyed by ordinary damage. If broken, time resumes immediately and the watch repairs itself after 7 days.

entries.name: Drawn Object
entries: As an action, draw one simple nonmagical object on a flat surface. The drawing becomes a real object at the end of the action, provided the object is no larger than Small, has no moving mechanical parts, and is worth 10 gp or less. The object lasts for 1 hour before reverting to a drawing.

The pencil cannot create food, currency, precious materials, weapons that deal damage, poisons, or objects intended to cause direct harm. The object appears in an unoccupied space adjacent to the drawing.

entries.name: Ink Supply
entries: The pencil can be used to create up to three objects, after which it regains all uses at dawn.

entries.name: Glimpse of the Future
entries: While wearing this hat, you can use an action to ask about a decision, action, or course of events that you expect to occur within the next 24 hours. The hat provides a brief, vague glimpse of one likely outcome, represented by a mental image, a symbolic vision, or a few words.

The vision reflects the most likely outcome based on circumstances at the time of use. It may reveal a potential danger, an opportunity, or an important consequence, but it does not reveal every detail and is not guaranteed to come true. Events and decisions that occur after the vision can change the future.
The DM determines the content of the vision. If the future is too uncertain, the hat may provide an unclear vision or indicate that several possible outcomes exist.

entries.name: Warning Antenna
entries: When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet is about to face an imminent danger, the antenna may twitch or emit a warning. This warning can alert you to danger within the next minute, but it does not reveal the exact nature, source, or timing of the threat.
Once you use Glimpse of the Future, you cannot use it again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Temporal Viewing
entries: As an action, choose a location on the same plane that you have seen before, or describe a specific historical event tied to a place you know. The screen shows a silent or audible view of that location at a time within the past 100 years, or up to 24 hours into the future. The viewing lasts up to 10 minutes.

The TV shows events from a fixed vantage point chosen by the DM. It cannot reveal a creature's thoughts, see through effects that block divination, or guarantee an accurate future if the future is changeable. The DM may provide only a partial view if the location or time is insufficiently specified.
Once used, this property cannot be used again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Portable Shelter
entries: As an action, place the shell on the ground and speak its command word. It unfolds into a small, sturdy house that can comfortably shelter up to six Medium creatures. The house contains a door, windows, basic furnishings, and a dry, climate-controlled interior.

The house is anchored to the ground and cannot be moved while expanded. As an action, you speak the command word again to collapse it into its portable shell, provided all creatures and objects have left it. The house has AC 15 and 50 hit points, and it is immune to poison and psychic damage.
The shell can be expanded once per day and remains expanded for up to 12 hours.

entries.name: Look Like a Stone
entries: As an action, pull the hat over your head and crouch or remain still. Until you move, speak above a whisper, or take an action, casual observers have difficulty distinguishing you from an ordinary roadside stone. A creature actively searching the area can identify you with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check.
This effect does not make you invisible, silence you, or conceal your presence from creatures that can sense you by smell, tremorsense, or other nonvisual means.

entries.name: Arrow of Love
entries: This magical arrow deals no damage. As an action, you can fire the arrow from a bow at two creatures you can see within the bow's normal range. The arrow magically affects both targets without requiring an attack roll, provided both targets are valid creatures.

Each target must make a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw. If both targets fail, they fall deeply in love with each other for 24 hours. Each creature regards the other as its beloved and seeks its company, attention, and affection. This effect does not compel either creature to obey the other or perform actions that directly endanger itself.
If only one target fails its saving throw, the effect does not take hold on either creature. If either target succeeds, both creatures are unaffected.
The effect ends early if either creature is harmed by the other. When the effect ends, both creatures realize that their feelings were magically influenced.
The arrow is consumed when fired, whether the targets are affected or not.

item.name: Hashirama Cells
entries: These cultivated cells originate from Hashirama Senju, the legendary shinobi whose vitality and Wood Release were beyond ordinary human limits. Implanting them into a creature's body grants extraordinary regenerative power, but the cells may overwhelm an incompatible host.

entries.name: Cellular Rejection
entries: When these cells are implanted, you must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or suffer rejection. On a failure, you take 6d6 necrotic damage, gain 1d4 levels of exhaustion, and the cells die, losing all their properties. The dead cells cannot be revived or restored. To gain the benefits of Hashirama Cells, you must obtain a new viable sample and undergo the implantation procedure again.

entries.name: Cellular Regeneration
entries: At the start of each of your turns during combat, if you have at least 1 hit point, you regain hit points equal to your character level + your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 hit point).
Outside of combat, if you have at least 1 hit point, you regain hit points equal to your proficiency bonus every 10 minutes.
If you have 0 hit points but are not dead, your cells continue to regenerate. You regain hit points equal to your proficiency bonus every 10 minutes. This regeneration stops if you die.

entries.name: Cellular Vitality
entries: Your hit point maximum increases by an amount equal to twice your character level when you receive these cells. Whenever you gain a level, your hit point maximum increases by an additional 2 hit points.

entries.name: Undying Cell
entries: Your body is exceptionally resilient against death. You gain expertise in death saving throws, meaning you add twice your proficiency bonus to death saving throws.

entries.name: Wood Release
entries: The power of Hashirama's cells grants you the ability to cast certain spells. You learn the spells listed below when you reach the specified character level. You can cast each spell once without expending a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest. You do not need material components when casting these spells through this trait.

items: Character level 1: {@spell Druidcraft}
Character level 2: {@spell Goodberry}
Character level 3: {@spell Spike Growth}
Character level 5: {@spell Plant Growth}
Character level 7: {@spell Grasping Vine}
Character level 9: {@spell Tree Stride}
Character level 11: {@spell Wall of Thorns}
Character level 13: {@spell Regenerate}
Character level 15: {@spell Clone}
Character level 17: {@spell Imprisonment}

item.name: Sharingan
entries: The Sharingan is a powerful ocular ability belonging to the Uchiha bloodline. Its abilities develop through combat and significant experiences, allowing the wielder to awaken increasingly powerful stages of the eye.

entries.name: One-Tomoe Sharingan
entries: Your Sharingan awakens in its initial form, granting you the following benefits:

items: You gain darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. If you already have darkvision, its range increases by 30 feet instead.
You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.
You can discern fine visual details and follow subtle movements with supernatural precision. You have advantage on the first attack roll you make against a creature during each of your turns.

entries: Your Sharingan evolves when you experience significant events during combat. It can advance directly to a higher stage without awakening the previous stages, depending on the event that occurs.
When you defeat a hostile creature while at least one allied creature you can see is bloodied, your Sharingan advances to the Two-Tomoe Sharingan.

entries.name: Two-Tomoe Sharingan
entries: Your Sharingan develops a second tomoe, improving your ability to perceive and predict movement.
You retain the benefits of the One-Tomoe Sharingan and gain the following additional benefits:
You have advantage on initiative rolls.
You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or against spells and other effects that create illusions.
When an allied creature you can see is reduced to 0 hit points, your Sharingan advances to the Three-Tomoe Sharingan.

entries.name: Three-Tomoe Sharingan
entries: Your Sharingan reaches its fully developed form, granting you exceptional perception and the ability to anticipate your opponents' movements.
You retain the benefits of the One-Tomoe and Two-Tomoe Sharingan.
You can cast {@spell suggestion} without expending a spell slot. Once you cast the spell in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

When a creature you can see makes its first attack roll against you during each round of combat, that attack roll has disadvantage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.
When an allied creature you can see dies, your Sharingan advances to the Mangekyō Sharingan.

entries.name: Mangekyō Sharingan Awakening
entries: When your Sharingan evolves into the Mangekyō Sharingan, roll 1d6 on the following table to determine the abilities awakened in your left and right eyes.

item.name: Mangekyō Sharingan
entries: The Mangekyō Sharingan is an advanced form of the Sharingan, granting its wielder powerful ocular abilities at the cost of the eyes' durability. Its powers include enhanced perception, powerful genjutsu, reality-altering techniques, and Susanoo.

entries.name: Sharingan Energy and Durability
entries: Your left and right eyes each have a maximum Sharingan Durability equal to 10 times your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1).
Your maximum Sharingan Energy is equal to half the sum of your left and right maximum Sharingan Durability, rounded down.
When you finish a short rest, you regain Sharingan Energy equal to 20 percent of your maximum Sharingan Energy, rounded down.
When you finish a long rest, you regain Sharingan Energy equal to your maximum Sharingan Energy.
Whenever an ability reduces your Sharingan Durability, reduce the Sharingan Durability of both your left and right eyes by the specified amount.

Your Sharingan Durability can't be restored by resting or other ordinary means. Once either eye's Sharingan Durability is depleted, that eye must be replaced with another Mangekyō Sharingan eye through transplantation.

entries.name: Enhanced Sharingan
entries: You can discern fine visual details and follow subtle movements with supernatural precision. You gain the following benefits:
You gain darkvision out to a range of 120 feet. If you already have darkvision, its range increases by 60 feet instead.
You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.
You have advantage on the first attack roll you make against a creature during each of your turns.
You have advantage on initiative rolls.
You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed and against spells and other effects that create illusions.
You can cast {@spell suggestion} without expending a spell slot at will.
When a creature you can see makes its first attack roll against you during each round of combat, that attack roll has disadvantage.

entries.name: Enhanced Visual Perception
entries: At the start of your turn, you can expend 3 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of both your left and right eyes by 1 to heighten your visual perception until the start of your next turn. For the duration, you have advantage on all attack rolls you make and all saving throws you make, and attack rolls against you have disadvantage.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

entries.name: Izanagi
entries: As a reaction, you can use Izanagi to alter the outcome of an event affecting yourself, treating an unfavorable outcome as an illusion and rewriting reality in your favor.

After using Izanagi, the eye used to activate this ability becomes permanently blind, and its Sharingan Durability is reduced to 0. This blindness can't be removed by resting or ordinary healing. The eye must be replaced through transplantation to restore vision.

entries.name: Izanami
entries: As a reaction, you can use Izanami to trap a creature in a repeating sequence of events, forcing it to experience a loop until it accepts the truth underlying the illusion.

After using Izanami, the eye used to activate this ability becomes permanently blind, and its Sharingan Durability is reduced to 0. This blindness can't be removed by resting or ordinary healing. The eye must be replaced through transplantation to restore vision.

entries.name: Tailed Beast Genjutsu
entries: You can expend 10 Sharingan Energy to attempt to control a creature of the Beast or Monstrosity type that you can see. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your feature save DC. On a failed save, the target must obey your commands while the genjutsu remains active.
Whenever you take damage, the affected creature can repeat the Wisdom saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.
The genjutsu ends if your Sharingan Energy is depleted.

entries.name: Skeletal Susanoo
entries: You can activate Skeletal Susanoo at any time by expending 10 Sharingan Energy and reducing the Sharingan Durability of both your left and right eyes by 2. You don't need to pay the maintenance cost on the turn you activate it. Starting at the beginning of your next turn, you can expend 10 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of both your left and right eyes by 2 to maintain it.
When you activate this Susanoo, you gain temporary hit points equal to 10 times your proficiency bonus.
While this Susanoo is active, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a +5 bonus to AC.
You gain a +2 bonus to all saving throws.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls.
The save DC of your features and spells increases by 1.
At the start of each of your turns while this Susanoo is active, you gain temporary hit points equal to 10 times your proficiency bonus, replacing any temporary hit points you currently have.

entries: You can end Skeletal Susanoo at any time, requiring no action. If you can't pay the Sharingan Energy or Sharingan Durability cost to maintain it, the form ends automatically.

entries.name: Armored Susanoo
entries: You can activate Armored Susanoo at any time by expending 25 Sharingan Energy and reducing the Sharingan Durability of both your left and right eyes by 5. You don't need to pay the maintenance cost on the turn you activate it. Starting at the beginning of your next turn, you can expend 15 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of both your left and right eyes by 3 to maintain it.
When you transform into Armored Susanoo, you gain temporary hit points equal to 25 times your proficiency bonus.
While this Susanoo is active, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a +10 bonus to AC.
You gain a +5 bonus to all saving throws.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls.
The save DC of your features and spells increases by 3.
At the start of each of your turns while this Susanoo is active, you gain temporary hit points equal to 25 times your proficiency bonus, replacing any temporary hit points you currently have.

entries: You can end Armored Susanoo at any time, requiring no action. When you end Armored Susanoo, you revert to Skeletal Susanoo if you can still maintain it; otherwise, Susanoo ends. If you can't pay the Sharingan Energy or Sharingan Durability cost to maintain Armored Susanoo, the form ends automatically.

entries.name: Mangekyō Sharingan Awakening
entries: When your Sharingan evolves into the Mangekyō Sharingan, roll 1d6 on the following table to determine the abilities awakened in your left and right eyes. The specific mechanics and costs of these abilities are determined separately.

entries.name: Mangekyō Sharingan Signature
entries: Each Mangekyō Sharingan awakens unique ocular abilities known as Signature Abilities. These powers embody the wielder's unique visual prowess, granting extraordinary control over flames, space, time perception, and the minds of others. Each ability is tied to a specific eye and may carry a terrible cost.

entries.name: Amaterasu
entries: As a action, You expend 15 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of the eye used by 5 to unleash the black flames of Amaterasu upon a target you can see. The target is engulfed in black flames and immediately takes fire damage equal to a number of d12s equal to your proficiency bonus.

At the start of each of the target's turns, the target takes fire damage from Amaterasu, and the damage increases by 1d12 after each instance of damage. The black flames do not extinguish themselves, and this effect continues until the target dies, you extinguish the flames, or the target escapes them using an appropriate ability.
A creature can end the effect on itself by severing or removing the body part engulfed in the flames, if physically possible. The DM determines the consequences of doing so.

A creature can also escape the flames by using a teleportation ability, such as {@spell misty step}, to move away from them. The effect ends on that creature, but the flames remain where they were left.
Resistance to fire damage does not extinguish the black flames or end this effect. Immunity to fire damage instead grants resistance to the fire damage dealt by Amaterasu.

entries.name: Kagutsuchi
entries: Kagutsuchi grants you control over the black flames of Amaterasu, allowing you to shape, manipulate, and weaponize them with extraordinary precision. You gain the following abilities:

entries.name: Black Flame Infusion
entries: You can use your bonus action to expend 25 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of both your left and right eyes by 5 to unleash the black flames of Amaterasu.

The next time you deal damage to a creature with a weapon, spell, or other feature, you infuse your attack with the black flames. The target takes additional fire damage from Amaterasu as if it had been hit by Amaterasu directly. This damage uses the damage progression described in the Amaterasu feature. The infusion ends after dealing this additional damage.

If black flames created by Amaterasu are already burning within your line of sight, regardless of their source, you can instead use this feature by expending 10 Sharingan Energy and reducing the Sharingan Durability of the eye used by 5.

entries.name: Black Flame Armor
entries: When you are hit by a melee attack, you can use your reaction to expend 25 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of both your left and right eyes by 5 to engulf yourself in the black flames of Amaterasu.
The attacker takes fire damage from Amaterasu as if it had been hit by Amaterasu directly. This damage uses the damage progression described in the Amaterasu feature.

If black flames created by Amaterasu are already burning within your line of sight, regardless of their source, you can instead use this feature by expending 10 Sharingan Energy and reducing the Sharingan Durability of the eye used by 5.

entries.name: Control Black Flame
entries: If black flames created by Amaterasu are burning within your line of sight, regardless of their source, you can use a bonus action to expend 10 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of the eye used by 5 to control and manipulate those flames. You can move or reshape the existing flames without needing to create them again.

When you move the flames onto a creature, make a ranged spell attack against that creature using your Primary Ability for the attack roll. On a hit, the creature is engulfed in the black flames and takes fire damage from Amaterasu as if it had been hit by Amaterasu directly. This damage uses the damage progression described in the Amaterasu feature.

entries.name: Tsukuyomi
entries: Tsukuyomi traps a target within a powerful illusion that distorts its perception of time and reality, allowing the wielder to inflict profound psychological torment within moments.

entries.name: Kamui
entries: Kamui grants access to a separate dimension, allowing the wielder to transport creatures or objects between dimensions and, depending on the awakened eye, phase through attacks or warp targets away.

entries.name: Ōhirume
entries: Ōhirume allows the wielder to create and manipulate black gravitational spheres, exerting immense attraction and controlling their movement to restrain or crush targets.

entries.name: Kotoamatsukami
entries: Kotoamatsukami is an extraordinarily subtle genjutsu that alters a target's thoughts and decisions without the target realizing that its mind has been manipulated.

entries.name: Transplantation
entries: You can attempt to replace a blinded Mangekyō Sharingan eye with another Mangekyō Sharingan eye. The transplantation requires a successful DC 20 Constitution saving throw.
On a success, the transplantation succeeds. On a failure, the transplanted eye becomes permanently blind and can't be used.
